order.why: Rule 1 clean deg-3: two short proton stubs peaking at 220k and 240k rise away, plus the 20011+20013+20009 chain is one 128 cm muon with a textbook template Bragg reaching 245k at 20003.

Rule 1 seen only in the zoom: 19006 is a real 3-prong knot with a 1.8 cm 207936 e/cm proton stub and a short e stub beside the long pion, while the apparent kink at 19005 is 169 deg, i.e. a scatter on the same 139 cm track that stops with a Michel far downstream.

Rule 8: the longest cluster is 8.5 cm and the event is two loose scatters of sub-cm blobs with no connected structure and no readable direction, so any click is as good as any other and I abstain rather than invent a reason.
Rules 1 and 3: three prongs at a wide V, the 4.4 cm proton rises away, and the 56 cm pi+ has a textbook Bragg at 8005 followed by a mu-then-e decay chain, so 8005 is the far end.
Rule 8: the whole event is a scatter of sub-5cm fragments spread over 60cm in x and 30cm in z with no track, no cone and no readable direction, so any click is as good as any other and I abstain.

Trap 3 kills the apparent rule-1 winner 11004 (170 deg pair and the zoom shows literally no kink), so the cluster is one 84 cm track; rule 3 puts the Michel-like 5 cm stub at 11003, making 11001 the start end.

Rule 1 + rule 2: the 260cm track has a genuine template-following Bragg rise over its last 15cm at 18005, which fixes its direction as +z from 18004, and 18004 is by far the lowest-z candidate; unclear because 18004 sits on the upstream z=0 face, where an entering particle looks identical.

Cluster 18 is a dead-straight 298cm MIP from the y- wall to the x- wall with no prong and no Bragg anywhere, so no vertex structure in it; only other object is this 3.8cm 82k blob, chosen over the two smaller blobs, essentially a guess.

Rule 7: compact all-electron tangle with no readable track direction; cone opening rises fastest and most monotonically from 18004 (far-near +3.6 cm vs +2.1 for the other deg-3 hub 18005, 2.6 cm away).

Rule 3: p4 shows the 228 cm muon falling from 185k right at 2000 along the stopping template, and two Michel-like blobs (19002, 20004) sit on that same end, so 2000 is the far end and the MIP end 2001 at z=244 is the vertex.

Rule 1 with p4 shape: dQ/dx follows the stopping-proton template monotonically from 205604 at 6000 down to ~116000 at the far end, so the particle starts at the cool end; the 161 deg break at 6002 is a scatter within one 23.6 cm proton, which is why I take 6001 rather than 6002 (2.5 cm apart).

12000 is the only candidate with rule-1 support (52 cm track starts sub-MIP there and rises to a Bragg at the floor), but a 5 cm 4x-MIP proton stub with several blips sits 44 cm away and is an equally plausible vertex region.

Rule-1 trap: the only deg-3 candidate 17004 is a 3 cm delta-ray split on an exactly collinear (180 deg) flat-MIP track running wall to wall, so I took instead the contained low-z end of the isolated 26 cm MIP that sits inside the sub-cm fragment cloud.

The only real cluster is a 335 cm track that is flat MIP for 320 cm and then follows the stopping-muon template up to 270k at 16001, so rule 1 puts the origin at 16000 - but 16000 sits on the z=498 downstream face, which would require a backward-going muon, and the only other structure is a handful of sub-cm 13k blobs 30-40 cm off the stopping end with no readable topology.

Only 8 cm of charge at the top wall; dQ/dx rises upward (57k to 83k) so the lower end 2000 is the start by rule 1, but a 0.9 cm blob sits 7 cm further down on the same vertical line and could be the true start.
Rule 1 textbook: deg-3 with 3 of 3 segments rising away - 427 cm muon (x1.84), 8.3 cm proton to 188k (x1.45) and 15.1 cm pi+ (x1.36); zoom shows three well-separated green arrows, nothing collinear.

The zoom shows dQ/dx rising monotonically along the whole chain 22001 -> 22002 -> 22000, so cluster 22 is one fully contained 64 cm stopping particle whose Bragg is at 22000; both ends are interior, making 22001 the cool start and the only contained-track vertex in the event.

Whole event is one collinear 110cm chain; 4108 is rule-1 negative (0 of 3 away, 1 toward) so I dropped it, and I could not decide whether cluster 4's stopping track is a product of a vertex at 4014 or a particle entering at the x=-200 wall; 75085 wins on the two quantified rules (strongest rise-away in the event, x2.21, and lowest z) and is the apex of the cluster-75 spray.

Deg-4 blob junction: the 4.3 cm proton falls 78k to 42k toward 11004 (born there) and both the 14.9 cm e prong and the 1.3 cm stub attach at 11004 only; held to likely because the mu and pi+ arms leave it collinear to 2 deg, which is trap 3.
Rule 1 with p4 shape: textbook stopping profile, flat MIP for 47 cm then a monotone Bragg to 250000 at 12005, so the cool 56793 end 12000 is where the particle started.

The Michel shower (cluster 62) sitting on a genuine monotone Bragg rise at 1001 fixes that as the stopping end (rule 3), and the trajectory through 1002 is a smooth arc with no kink, so the track starts at 1000, where the high 5 cm mean is only a 1-2 point spike.

Rule 1: 352 cm muon is flat MIP with no Bragg at either end (exits at x=200/z=500 corner) and the 11 cm proton rises monotonically 80k->280k away from 16002 to its Bragg at 16001; prongs 79 deg apart.

Rule 7 plus rule 1: 16001 is the narrow apex of the EM shower that opens from 16 cm wide at z=220 to 32 cm wide at z=237, and the 13.5 cm stalk cools toward it (62860 far, 51625 here); the rival 25007 is 6.7 cm away, does not touch it in the tight zoom, and is the HOT end of its own segment.

The 357 cm spine is one straight track (successive segment directions agree to 2.6 and 4.5 deg, so the collinearity trap disqualifies 17010/17004/17006, and p4 shows 17004's 96k is a delta spike that falls back to 30k); the far end 17003 has the real Bragg plus an 8.3 cm Michel, leaving the MIP start 17001.

Rule 1 on the only fitted object: the 42 cm track shows a clean monotone template-following Bragg rise (50k to 245k over the last 3.5 cm) at 9001, so it is the stopping end and the track cools all the way toward 9000; low confidence because that leaves a single prong with no second prong anywhere and the remaining candidates are structureless sub-cm blips.

Deg-3 point where a 7.8 cm prong genuinely originates (28k at the junction rising to 80k where it stops), while the 158 cm MIP passes straight through it at 175.7 deg, which drops the tier per trap 3.

A 135 cm track runs from the anode wall to this interior end; p4 shows the apparent rise at 22000 is one hot bin and not a monotone Bragg, so this is equally a stopping cosmic with a Michel (the 2.5 cm e-stub 7 cm away) as it is a vertex.

Rule 1 3 of 3 rising away: the 72 cm proton falls from 190k at its stop at 11000 back to 78k here, the 62 cm muon leaves at MIP and Braggs to 170k at 11003, and the 28 cm pi+ leaves cool; p1 shows a clean three-pronged star.

Rule 1 via p4: the 29 cm muon's last points at the 12003 end spike to ~160000 straight onto the stopping-muon template, and 12003 is degree 1 so nothing can bleed charge into it, so 12003 is the stop and the vertex is 12002, whose own 5 cm mean is inflated by its 1.6 cm second prong.

Rule 6 by elimination: cluster 18 is a 178 deg flat-MIP wall-to-wall track and the 209 cm track is flat MIP starting exactly on the z=0 face, so the only convergence is at 23005 where a hot 9.7 cm proton-like segment and four small fragments cluster; the backward-muon reading keeps me from calling it likely.

Only genuine junction in a diffuse event: three prongs, the 4.4 cm one rising monotonically 33k->118k to a stopping end at 21013 and the 17.6 cm one also rising away; the two hot proton stubs 150 cm away share no common point (15 cm apart, unaligned).

The 85cm track is flat MIP with no Bragg, so the 195k point at 9002 with its 2.7cm 165k proton stub and half a dozen small blobs within 30cm is vertex activity; the other end 9001 sits on the z=0 face.

Clusters 9 and 61 are one ~32cm stopping proton (dQ/dx 52k at 9000 to 125k at 9001 to 240k at 61053, matching the proton range-energy curve), so its cool end 9000 is the start; shower fragments 58/46030/45028 sit within 6cm of it.
Rule 1, 2 of 2 with real template Bragg peaks at both far ends: 108 cm muon rising to 215k at 7004 and 46 cm proton rising to 235k at 7003, with a 112 deg opening so trap 3 does not apply.

Rule 8 territory - almost no charge in the event; picked the very hot sub-cm proton-like deposit at the lowest z (7.4 cm) over the only alternative, a sub-MIP 7.6 cm fragment lying on the y=200 top wall. Close to a guess.
